contributions.quote: Our contributions are three. First, a generator that targets surviving mutants. Second, a check that reruns each new test to find flaky ones. Third, an evaluation on 30 open-source projects.
contributions.text: The paper claims three contributions: a test generator that targets surviving mutants, a check that reruns each new test to detect flaky ones, and an evaluation on 30 open-source projects.

contributions.quote: Kothden found 18 percent more seeded faults than a random baseline, at the same time budget.
contributions.text: Kothden is reported to find 18 percent more seeded faults than a random baseline under the same time budget on 30 open-source projects.

contributions.quote: Kothden also records which generated tests fail intermittently and reports them as flaky.
contributions.text: Kothden also records generated tests that fail intermittently and reports them as flaky rather than discarding them.

evaluation.quote: For each project we seed faults with a different mutation tool than the one used for guidance, and we give Kothden and a random baseline the same ten-minute budget.
evaluation.text: The evaluation seeds faults on 30 Java projects using a different mutation tool than the one used for guidance, giving Kothden and a random baseline the same ten-minute budget. It reports 42 flaky tests, 37 confirmed by hand.

prior_work.quote: Search-based test generation [1] optimizes coverage and does not use mutants. Studies of mutation analysis [2] motivate our use of mutants.
prior_work.text: The paper positions search-based generation [1] as coverage-optimizing without mutants, cites mutation-analysis studies [2] as motivation, and notes flaky-test work [3] measures prevalence whereas Kothden detects flakiness during generation.

closest_cited_work.text: Search-based generation of unit tests for object-oriented programs; Kothden uses a genetic algorithm in the style of this earlier work.
closest_cited_work.quote: using a genetic algorithm in the style of earlier work [1]
